title: Scott and Seymour's tournament-local chromatic number conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a graph and $T$ a tournament on the same vertex set. For a vertex $v$, write $N_T^+(v)$ for its out-neighbourhood in $T$.

**Scott and Seymour's conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$ there exists a positive integer $\chi$ such that, for every graph $G$ with $\chi(G) \geqslant \chi$ and every tournament $T$ on the same vertex set, there is a vertex $v$ such that

$$
\chi(G[N_T^+(v)])\geqslant k.
$$

The paper disproves this conjecture, so the proposed implication does not hold in general.
source_name: António Girão, Kevin Hendrey, Freddie Illingworth, Florian Lehner, Lukas Michel, Michael Savery and Raphael Steiner, “Chromatic number is not tournament-local”, arXiv:2305.15585 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.15585

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2023). “This conjecture remained open for two decades and was first proved by Lov\'{a}sz using homotopy theory (see also B\'{a}r\'{a}ny and Greene for very short proofs).”
